aspects.says: close() on a decorator flushes it and closes the stream it wraps, so closing the outermost stream writes every layer's bytes and closes everything below, while closing or flushing only an inner layer leaves data behind.
basis: section:Each Layer Can Hold Bytes, So Only Closing the Outermost Stream Writes Them All

aspects.says: Map's default compound methods make no atomicity guarantee, so through a decorator that doesn't override them, concurrent updates are lost.
basis: section:A Decorator That Doesn't Override a Default Method Runs the Interface's Code, Not the Wrapped Object's

aspects.says: A default method the decorator doesn't override runs the interface's code on the decorator, so the wrapped object's override, such as an atomic computeIfAbsent or a batch call, is never reached.
basis: section:A Decorator That Doesn't Override a Default Method Runs the Interface's Code, Not the Wrapped Object's

aspects.says: A decorator is a different object: the JDK's List, Set and Map wrappers forward equals and hashCode, while unmodifiableCollection and synchronizedCollection keep Object's identity.
basis: section:A Decorator Is Another Object: equals Is Forwarded Only Where the Interface Defines It

aspects.says: GZIPOutputStream.finish() completes the compressed data and writes the trailer without closing, but only for what has reached it: layers above must be flushed before it and layers below after it.
basis: section:finish() Completes the GZIP Data Without Closing, but Only What Has Reached the Compressor

aspects.says: Overriding the default to forward straight to the wrapped object keeps its behaviour but skips the decorator's own work, so the override must forward and decorate.
basis: section:A Decorator That Doesn't Override a Default Method Runs the Interface's Code, Not the Wrapped Object's

aspects.says: A decorator acts on the calls it receives: a buffer above a compressor cuts the calls into it, and a buffer below it cuts the writes reaching the file.
basis: section:Buffer Above the Compressor: the Order Decides How Many Calls Reach Each Layer
